blog_summary: Adrian Colyer highlights Rosetta, Facebook's production-scale OCR system for extracting text from images uploaded to social media platforms. The system processes hundreds of millions of images daily using a two-step pipeline: text detection followed by text recognition. The detection model uses Faster-RCNN (via Facebook's Detectron platform) to identify text regions, leveraging ShuffleNet for speed. For recognition, a fully-convolutional CTC-based model handles variable-length text, including non-dictionary words like URLs or emails. The authors address real-world challenges like noisy detection outputs and diverse languages by training on multiple datasets and employing curriculum learning. The system is deployed in production, demonstrating scalability and robustness.
paper_title: Rosetta: large scale system for text detection and recognition in images
